title: Redesigning a Failing Product
paragraphs: After her team's flagship product experienced consistently declining sales for three consecutive quarters, Widad faced pressure to either significantly discount the existing product or invest substantial remaining budget into a complete redesign.

Rather than choosing between these two options immediately, she insisted on conducting thorough customer research first, an approach some board members considered an unnecessary delay given the product's clearly worsening financial trajectory.

This research revealed that customers valued the product's core functionality considerably, but found a specific, relatively minor interface issue frustrating enough to actively seek alternatives from competing companies instead.

Rather than the complete redesign originally proposed, Widad's team implemented a targeted fix addressing this specific frustration, preserving the substantial remaining budget while directly addressing the actual underlying customer concern.

Sales recovered significantly within two quarters following this targeted intervention, considerably faster than a complete redesign would have realistically allowed given typical development timelines for comparable products.

Widad later presented this experience at an internal conference, emphasizing that thorough diagnosis before committing significant resources often reveals more precise, cost-effective solutions than initial assumptions about necessary interventions might suggest.
